description:
Existing Telegram real-attachment regression cannot obtain transport requirements from the installed Jido.Chat.Telegram.Adapter (dependency jido_chat_telegram 1.2.1). Code.ensure_loaded!/1 plus function_exported?(..., :file_requirements, 1) returns false. At baseline 14fee186e, JidoChatBridge.adapter_file_requirements returns unsupported when callback is absent; FileRequirements.validate(nil) produces configuration failure and direct planner default :abort rejects the attempt. The existing TelegramHistoryDeliveryTest document-byte assertion therefore conflicts with that baseline contract. zaq-1lw.20 retains the assertion; its agreed consistent default :continue now reports a partial text-only configuration outcome instead of guessing limits.

Scope here is investigation/contract agreement only until separately authorized. Determine supported provider requirements contract, source accurate limits without guessing, and decide ownership/pinned dependency adoption. Do not weaken or skip the existing sendDocument/exact-byte assertions, silently rename upstream callbacks, publish dependencies, or add host fallback limits merely to pass tests.

Validation: existing test/zaq/channels/telegram_history_delivery_test.exs: real document bytes, filename, caption, confirmed provider ID and no duplicate sends; then relevant Jido requirements and channel suites. Action reuse assessment: inspect existing adapter.file_requirements/1 and host transport_requirements/2 normalization; extend the existing provider/bridge contract rather than a parallel delivery path. Requires separate agreed behavior and existing-test expectation approval if any expectations change. No dependency or code publication authorized.

comments.text: Baseline execution reproduced in an isolated Elixir VM: loaded original Outgoing, FileRequirements, Step, DeliveryPlan, DeliveryFiles and JidoChatBridge from HEAD=14fee186e with unchanged installed dependencies, then sent a synthetic Telegram attachment without network I/O. Result: {:error, DeliveryError{reason: :invalid_file_requirements, stage: :configuration, delivery: :not_sent}}. Current adapter callback export check is false. This proves the existing real-document test conflict predates zaq-1lw.20. Probe source stayed under /tmp and no baseline module was written into repository/build BEAM files.

User reported telegram_history_delivery_test.exs:38 and explicitly approved test migration in current session: keep accepted missing file_requirements adapter limitation, move exact bytes/name/caption assertions to the real adapter document operation, and separately assert bridge missing-requirements fallback. No invented host limits, dependency edits or pin changes. Baseline reproduced: partial text message, no delivered attachments, configuration failure. Reuse installed Extensions.send_document and existing DocumentTransport plus the actual Jido bridge for fallback; test-only, no new Action/tool/host transport. Preserve provider-ID, exact bytes, caption and duplicate-send coverage at the supported boundaries. Keep upstream adoption gap tracked; no commit/push.

Approved migration implemented: exact binary <<255,0,128>>, image.png filename, Image as a file caption, provider message ID101 and one sendDocument call are asserted through real Telegram Adapter.send_file/3 using FileUpload(kind: :file). Added actual bridge regression verifying missing requirements produce partial text-only delivery with original answer, configuration/not_sent failure at index0, no uploaded or delivered file refs, one HTTP sendMessage, and abort policy rejects before HTTP. No wrapper adapter, invented limits, dependency edits or production changes. Existing history/edit tests retained.

Telegram migration validated in both complete reported modules (22 PASS) and related regression suite (395 PASS,12 properties). Exact document payload/ID/no-duplicate assertions and bridge continue/abort missing-requirements assertions all pass. Limitation intentionally remains: installed adapter does not expose file_requirements/1; upstream adapter/pin adoption stays deferred rather than inventing host limits. No commits/pushes.
Final mix q and diff checks PASS after approved test migration. Validation logs shared with .33; no dependency or production edits. Adapter limitation intentionally retained.

User explicitly requested complete removal of the direct-adapter document test because it bypasses the executor and gives a false impression of ZAQ Telegram file-delivery coverage. This supersedes the prior approval to retain exact-byte coverage through Adapter.send_file. Remove that test plus its now-unused DocumentTransport fixture and FileUpload alias. Retain actual bridge/executor text-fallback and stop-policy regression plus existing Telegram history/edit tests. Full attachment executor-path support remains absent/deferred. Action reuse not applicable: test deletion only; no executable production operation changes. Run remaining Telegram suite and mix q; preserve all other workspace changes, no commit/push.

Removed direct-adapter exact-document test completely, along with its unused DocumentTransport module and FileUpload alias, as explicitly requested. Actual bridge/executor fallback and abort regression remains. Remaining Telegram suite:6 PASS; mix q PASS; git diff --check PASS. Logs /tmp/zaq-telegram-test-removal-tests.log and /tmp/zaq-telegram-test-removal-quality.log. All other workspace edits preserved; no commit/push. Earlier direct-adapter byte-check validation is historical and must not be represented as current ZAQ executor-path coverage.

Requested direct-adapter test removal and retained bridge fallback/abort regression published in 17eb5d84d on origin/feat/channel-files with user authorization. Installed Telegram attachment requirements limitation remains; no adapter/pin changes or full file executor support claimed.

title: [zaq-1lw.21] Reconcile Telegram attachment transport requirements
